In this Chinese city, nine a.m. can still be dark.
In winter, the sun doesn't come up until after ten.
This is Kashgar, in China's far west.
The country is wide enough for about five time zones, but it all runs on one clock: Beijing time.
So many people here keep a second clock, Xinjiang time, two hours behind.
Say "see you at noon", and someone will ask: which noon?
Now imagine one place for every job and every agent.
